front.title: Constitution checks
front.md:
- **System shock** d% ≤ **95** — petrification and its reversal, polymorph (again on changing back), magical ageing, staying conscious
- **Resurrection** d% ≤ **96** — limit 16 revivals, −1 Con each
- **Holding breath** (underwater, swimming or diving) 6 rounds (3 exerting; halved without a good gulp of air); then a Con check each round, −2 cumulative after the first
- **Jog** 16 rounds, then a Con check each round · **Run** a check every round (−1 / −2 / −3 cumulative per round at ×3 / ×4 / ×5)
- **Force march** 30 mi a day; a check each night (−1 per day)
- **Swim** 16 hours at half speed or treading water; then a Con check each hour (−1 Con per hour); choppy water: a check every hour

front.title: Mounted combat
front.md:
*On Hotspur (DMG ch. 9; PHB, Charging). Riding check: d20 ≤ 15.*

- **In the saddle:** **+1 to hit** foes smaller than the horse (not riders, not giants); foes on foot **−1** to hit him (not the horse). Hotspur is war-trained: no penalty
- **Charge:** move +50%, attack at the end, **+2 to hit**; lance **double damage**. Foes −2 initiative; he loses Dex to AC and takes +1 — **AC 1** shielded, **4** other; a set spear or polearm does double damage to him
- **Lance:** heavy lance needs a heavy horse ✓ · strikes round 1, then every other round (break off, wheel, return) · drop it to fight close · may break on a hit
- **Bow from the saddle:** only while Hotspur **stands still** (on the move, long bows are for specialists only) — full rate, normal to hit
- **Unhorsed:** horse killed — Riding check to land on his feet, else fall (1d3), lose this round and the next · natural 20 from a rider's 3-ft+ weapon (footman's 10-ft+): knocked off (1d3) unless Riding check · lasso: Riding check to stop short · flying tackle: Dex check (≤ 16) to stay seated
- **Leap down and attack** a foe within 10 ft: Riding **≤ 11**

back.title: Special abilities and restrictions
back.md:
**Fighter, long sword specialist** — of the Greyhawk Surrounds. Arms of DeWitt: a white horse beneath a gold crown, on blue.

- **Weapons and armour:** any
- **Specialist (long sword):** +1 hit, +2 dmg; **3/2 attacks** a round (Fighter 1–6; 2 a round from Fighter 7)
- **Shield proficiency** (house rule): medium shield, 2 slots — +3 AC against 2 opponents a round; *knock back*. A third slot: +4 AC and the shield as an off-hand weapon (1d3 / 1d5)
- **Weapon slots:** 5 of 5 — long sword (2, specialised) · battle axe · medium shield (2). Non-proficient −2: bow, lance, dagger. Next slot at Fighter 6
- **Experience:** +10% (Strength 16+)
- **At 9th level:** a stronghold attracts men-at-arms and household guards
- **Saves improve** at Fighter 5: 11 / 13 / 12 / 13 / 14

back.title: Special abilities and restrictions
back.md:
**Specialty priest of Trithereon** — the Summoner; power of individuality and the right to self-protection. Symbol: the pursuit rune (triskelion). Raiment: blue robes.

- **No turning undead** (TU nil)
- **Weapons:** any — spear his first proficiency, broadsword his second
- **Armour:** chain only by the Atlas; leather also allowed (homebrew)
- **Spheres:** All · Astral · Combat · Guardian · Healing · Protection · Summoning · Travelers' — *minor (spell levels 1–3 only):* Chaos · Charm · Necromantic · Sun. **Also approved by the DM:** *Detect Magic*, *Dust Devil*, *Messenger*, *Snake Charm*. No special spells.
- **Granted powers:** 3rd — backstab with an edged weapon for double damage (**active**) · 5th — *monster summoning* from the wizard list as priest spells · 8th — *animal summoning I*
- **Prayer slots:** 1st **4** · 2nd **3** *(Wisdom bonus 3rd and 4th come at Cleric 5 and 7)*; texts in the Tass Prayer Book
- **The priesthood:** Trithereon is a law unto himself; his priests care little for others' attitudes and are suspicious of lawful priests, even lawful good. In the cities the priesthood teaches self-protection and weapon use, practises battle tactics, and recruits rangers and thieves to teach its priests covert conflict; in the countryside priests serve as spies and border skirmishers, keeping watch against despots and evil humanoids

| Skeleton, 1 HD | **T** |
| Zombie | **T** |
| Ghoul, 2 HD | 4 |
| Shadow, 3–4 HD | 7 |
| Wight, 5 HD | 10 |
| Ghast | 13 |
| Wraith, 6 HD | 16 |
| Mummy, 7 HD | 19 |
| Spectre, 8 HD | 20 |
| Vampire, 9 HD + | — |

Turns **2d6**, lowest HD first; one roll for all types.

back.title: Special abilities and restrictions
back.md:
**Specialty priest of Pelor** — the Sun God; Power of strength, light and healing. Raiment: yellow robes (gold-trimmed from 7th level).

- **Turns undead at +1 level** — as a 5th-level priest (front)
- **Weapons:** flail, mace, morningstar, staff, staff-sling — **short bow also approved by the DM**
- **Armour:** leather or chain
- **Spheres:** All · Charm · Creation · Elemental (air) · Guardian · Healing · Necromantic · Protection · Sun — *minor (spell levels 1–3 only):* Summoning · Wards. No special spells.
- **Granted powers:** 1st — healing spells do at least **median** healing: *cure light wounds* at least **5 hp**, *cure serious* 9, *cure critical* 16, *heal* all but 1–2 hp; *cure moderate wounds* at least **6** (**active**) · 5th — automatic saves vs spells that blind him (*darkness*, *blindness*) · 9th — *fly*
- **Prayer slots:** 1st **5** · 2nd **4** *(Wisdom bonus 3rd and 4th come at Cleric 5 and 7)*; texts in the Pelor Prayer Book
- **The priesthood:** Pelor's priests have always worked for the poor and sick, bringing healing, food and aid; quiet, kindly people for the most part, but with some steel as protection. Services: hymn-singing, communal prayer, alms to the needy (and their collection from the well-to-do). His reverence is turning more martial — a wrathful Power who drives out the darkness of evil

back.title: Prayers of his Faith
back.md:
*The DM-approved list for the levels he casts now.*

**1st level (22):** Antivermin Barrier · Bless/Curse · Blessed Watchfulness · Call Upon Faith · Combine · Command · Cure Light Wounds/Cause Light Wounds · Detect Magic · Dispel Fatigue · Endure Cold/Endure Heat · Invisibility to Undead · Light/Darkness · Orison · Protection from Evil/Protection from Good · Purify Food & Drink/Putrefy Food & Drink · Remove Fear/Cause Fear · Ring of Hands/Ring of Woe · Sacred Guardian · Sanctuary · Sunscorch · Weighty Chest · Wind Column

**2nd level (24):** Aid · Chant · Create Holy Symbol · Cure Moderate Wounds/Cause Moderate Wounds · Draw Upon Holy Might · Dust Devil · Enthrall · Ethereal Barrier · Frisky Chest · Hold Person · Iron Vigil · Messenger · Music of the Spheres · Mystic Transfer · Resist Acid and Corrosion · Resist Fire/Resist Cold · Restore Strength · Sanctify/Defile · Silence, 15' Radius · Slow Poison · Snake Charm · Withdraw · Wyvern Watch · Zone of Truth

back.title: Non-weapon proficiencies (5/8 slots)
back.md:
| Proficiency | Roll d20 ≤ | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Religion (Wis) | **18** | Ordinary facts of any faith of his homeland and its neighbours: automatic. Clergy, holy days: roll |
| Healing (Wis) | **16** | Within 1 round of the wound: **1d3 hp**, once per patient per day · in his care: 1 hp/day, 2 hp/day with full rest · up to 6 patients · poison through a wound: tend 5 rounds for **+2** to the save |
| Local History (Cha) | **10** | History of his home region · a tale that entertains needs no roll and gives **+2 Cha** for the encounter |

back.title: Languages known
back.md:
*No roll: languages are simply known. The DM may call a check only for a hard case (reading ≤ 13).*

- **Common** — native tongue: speaks it freely, no slot
- **Reading & writing Common** — Reading/Writing proficiency (1 slot)
- *3 non-weapon slots spare — a further language costs 1*

back.title: Homebrew rulings
back.md: Short bow approved by the DM as a weapon proficiency (outside Pelor's list) · **Shields (house rule):** +1 AC against a set number of opponents a round (medium: 2), front and shield side only; shield proficiency +1 more (medium, 1 slot) · *cure moderate wounds* at least 6 (DM) · Intelligence adds non-weapon proficiency slots, spendable on any proficiency (optional rule) · Comeliness carried as a house convention.

Astral Celerity.summary: While astral, your movement rate is doubled, you acclimatise quickly and you suffer no missile-fire penalties. On the Ethereal Plane it raises movement by half instead (12 becomes 18).

Battlefate.summary: Bends luck for one combatant, with a bonus of +1 per three caster levels (max +5 at 13th). Each round roll 1d6: 1 nothing, 2 AC, 3 saves, 4 attack rolls, 5 damage, 6 one extra attack using the bonus on attack or damage.

Bless/Curse.summary: Allies in the area who are not yet in melee gain +1 to attack rolls and +1 to morale and saves against fear; alternatively, blesses one item of up to 1 lb per level until used. Doesn't stack. Reverse: enemies suffer -1 to morale and attacks.

Blessed Watchfulness.summary: Keeps one sentry awake and alert: surprised only on a 1, treated as 4 levels or HD higher against sleep-type magic, and +2 to saves against charm, fear and other mind effects that would undermine the watch.

Call Upon Faith.summary: If the DM judges you to have kept faith, you gain +3 (or +15%) on one roll of your choice for an upcoming difficult task, such as a save, attack or ability check.

Combine.summary: Three to five priests link up: the highest-level one stands in the centre and gains one level per circling priest (max +4) for turning undead and level-based spell effects, but no extra spells. Circlers lose shield and Dex AC bonuses; if any loses concentration, it ends.

Command.summary: Speak one clear word in a language the target understands and it obeys for a round; 'Die!' makes it faint for a round, and self-destructive orders are ignored. No effect on undead. Creatures of Int 13+ or 6+ HD/levels get a save.

Cure Light Wounds/Cause Light Wounds.summary: Your touch heals 1d8 hit points to a living, corporeal creature that is not extraplanar. Reverse: inflicts 1d8 damage, needing an attack roll against an unwilling target.

Detect Magic.summary: Reveals magic in a strip ahead of you and how strong it is (dim to overwhelming); each level gives 10% to identify its sphere, but never its school. You can sweep a 60° arc each round; thick stone, metal or wood blocks it.

Dispel Fatigue.summary: Instantly clears all physical tiredness from one creature, leaving it fully rested and cancelling penalties from forced marching, swimming, running or accumulated fatigue points. Fatigue can build up again afterwards.

Invisibility to Undead.summary: Undead overlook the protected creature: those of 4 HD or less are automatically fooled, stronger ones save. Attacking ends it, though non-attack spells such as healing are fine, and a protected priest can't turn the fooled undead.

Know Direction.summary: You instantly learn which way is north, anywhere, including underground, underwater or in magical darkness.

Light/Darkness.summary: Creates torch-bright light in a 20-ft radius, fixed in place or on an object or creature (a creature may resist or save). Aimed at the eyes it blinds: -4 to attacks, saves and AC. Reverse: pitch-black magical darkness for half the duration; the two cancel.

Magical Stone.summary: Enchants up to three pebbles that anyone can throw (all in one round, to 30 yd) or sling proficiently. Each hit deals 1d4 (2d4 against undead) and counts as +1 magic for what it can hurt, with no attack or damage bonus. Lasts 30 minutes.

Mistaken Missive.summary: Ink on one page per level scrambles over six days, then settles into a legible message in the author's hand saying the opposite. Spellbook or scroll pages become a useless false spell of the same level. Dispel magic restores the text.

Orison.summary: Fills one 1st-level slot with several tiny prayers (3 + 1 per level, max 9), each chosen when cast: heal 1 hp, +1 to your next attack or next save vs magic or poison, calm fear, ease pain, sense nearby magic, or +2 to recall something.

Purify Food & Drink/Putrefy Food & Drink.summary: Makes up to 1 cu ft per level of spoiled, poisoned or contaminated food and water safe, though it can still rot later; it spoils unholy water. No effect on creatures or potions. Reverse: spoils food and drink, even holy water.

Remove Fear/Cause Fear.summary: Gives one creature per 4 levels +4 to saves against magical fear for a turn, and an immediate new save at +4 if they failed one today. Reverse: one creature flees in panic for 1d4 rounds unless it saves. Neither affects undead.

Sacred Guardian.summary: You know at once whenever the recipient is in danger, at any distance or even on another plane. From 3rd level you also receive a mental picture of the situation, but never its location.

Sanctuary.summary: Anyone trying to attack the warded creature directly must save vs spell or disregard it entirely; area attacks still work. The recipient may heal, bless, chant or cast divinations, but any offensive act ends the protection.

Speak with Astral Traveler.summary: By touching the body of someone away on an astral projection, you converse mind-to-mind with their travelling self, at ordinary speaking pace.

Sunscorch.summary: A ray of sunlight hits one creature for 1d6 + 1 per level (1d6 + 2 per level against undead and light-sensitive creatures), and living targets are blinded 1d4 rounds; a save dodges it. Needs open sky and the sun up; overcast is fine.

Aid.summary: Grants the benefits of bless (+1 to attacks and saves) plus 1d8 temporary hit points, which can take the recipient above their maximum, are lost first and cannot be healed back.

Astral Awareness.summary: Attunes you to Astral and Ethereal hazards such as conduits, psychic wind, cyclones, colour pools and curtains. 90% to spot a colour pool from behind, 5% per level to read its destination or sense ethereal gaze threats, +2 against planar surprise.

Aura of Comfort.summary: A shimmering aura keeps the recipient at a pleasant 70°F in natural temperatures from -20°F to 140°F and sheds rain, snow and hail; beyond that range it shifts by the excess. No protection from magical weather, fire, or fire or cold attacks.

Chant.summary: While you keep chanting and stand still, allies in the area gain +1 to attacks, damage and saves, and enemies suffer -1. Taking damage, being grappled or silenced breaks it. A same-faith priest's prayer spell alongside raises it to +2/-2.

Chaos Ward.summary: A whirling aura gives +1 AC in melee, and +2 AC and saves against missiles and spells aimed solely at the creature. For each such attack roll d% + caster level: 86–95 negated, 96–99 deflected to a random creature within 30 ft, 100+ reflected back.

Cure Moderate Wounds/Cause Moderate Woun.summary: Your touch heals 1d10+1 hit points to a living, corporeal creature that is not extraplanar. Reverse: a successful touch inflicts 1d10+1 damage.

Dissension's Feast.summary: Cast while preparing food (10 lb per level). Five rounds after eating, anyone who fails a save grows irritable, then quarrelsome and abusive, and all loyalties break down. When it ends they regain control but stay angry without knowing why.

Draw Upon Holy Might.summary: Boosts one of your Str, Dex, Con or Cha by +1 per three levels (max +6), even past racial or class limits, with full ability-score benefits. When it ends you collapse and can only rest for 4d6 turns (halved with a Con check).

Dust Devil.summary: Summons a small whirlwind (AC 4, 2 HD, MV 180 ft/round, 1d4 damage) that you direct; it vanishes if more than 30 yd from you. It snuffs small flames, pushes gas away, raises a blinding dust cloud on loose ground and can spoil spellcasting (save).

Enthrall.summary: After a round of uninterrupted speech, listeners who understand you must save or give you rapt attention while you keep talking (up to an hour), then 1d3 rounds more. Hostile races or faiths save at +4; 4+ HD or Wis 16+ are immune. Attacks break it.

Ethereal Barrier.summary: An unseen ward of two 10-ft squares per level, arranged as you like, that bars ethereal, phased, dimension-door and shadow-walk travel. It doesn't stop teleports, gates, astral beings or creatures that simply walk in. Several priests can pool their levels.

Hold Person.summary: Freezes 1d4 man-sized or smaller humans, demihumans or humanoids, who stay aware but cannot move or speak. Saves are normal against three or four targets, -1 against two, -2 against one. Undead are immune. You can end it with a word.

Iron Vigil.summary: You need no food or drink and are unharmed by natural heat, cold or exposure; you may meditate instead of sleeping (1-point penalty on surprise checks; sleep still needed to memorise spells). Afterwards you must eat and drink or make Con checks every 4 hours.

Lighten Load.summary: Halves the weight of a 10-ft cube's worth of gear, supplies or even an injured comrade, which can then be split among bearers or mounts. Size and use are unchanged. Doesn't work on magic items.

Messenger.summary: Lures a tiny, non-giant animal below Int 5 that fails a save; you can send it with a small note or item to a simply described place, where it waits until the spell ends. The recipient gains no way to talk with it.

Music of the Spheres.summary: Unearthly music entrances one listener per three levels (save negates): they cannot attack you and save at -3 against charm spells. Your companions get no protection, and any hostile act by you ends it. Targets must be able to hear it clearly.

Restore Strength.summary: Restores one creature's strength and stamina drained by magic or unnatural sources such as chill touch, ray of enfeeblement or a shadow's touch. Only temporary ability losses are fixed; natural fatigue, disease or injury are not helped.

Sanctify/Defile.summary: Hallows ground, alone or with other priests. Your deity's followers there gain +2 to saves against fear and charm, same-alignment allies +1, and hostile creatures suffer -1; priests there turn undead as one level higher. Reverse: same save effects, but turning is one level lower.

Silence, 15' Radius.summary: Total silence in the area: no speech, no verbal spells, no sound in or out. Can be centred on an object or creature so it moves with it (an unwilling creature that saves has it placed just behind). Blocks sound-based attacks.

Slow Poison.summary: Cast on a poisoned creature before the poison fully takes hold, it holds the venom at bay so it does no serious harm while the spell lasts, buying time for a cure. It does not neutralise the poison.

Snake Charm.summary: Sets snakes swaying harmlessly, up to a total of hit points equal to your own. Lasts 1d4+2 turns on dormant snakes, 1d3 turns on calm ones, 1d4+4 rounds on angry ones. Also works on snake-like monsters such as nagas, subject to magic resistance.

Spiritual Hammer.summary: A force hammer attacks any target you can see in range each round while you concentrate, using your THAC0 without Strength, at +1 per six levels (max +3) to hit and damage. Damage 1d4+1 (man-sized or smaller) or 1d4 (larger) plus bonus.

Wyvern Watch.summary: A faint wyvern shape guards a spot; the first intruder who fails a save is paralysed one round per level (until freed by you, dispel magic or remove paralysis), then the spell ends. Approachers may spot it: 90% in daylight, 30% at dusk, never in darkness.

Antivermin Barrier.summary: An invisible field keeps out non-magical insects, rodents, spiders, snakes and similar vermin under 1 HD, including summoned swarms. Vermin already inside are unaffected but cannot come back once they leave.

Endure Cold/Endure Heat.summary: The recipient is unharmed by natural cold down to -30°F or heat up to 130°F (choose one), taking 1 point per hour per degree beyond. Any magical heat or cold ends it, though the first 10 points of that damage are ignored.

Protection from Evil/Protection from Goo.summary: Evil attackers suffer -2 to hit and the recipient gains +2 to saves against them; mental control or possession is blocked, and summoned or extraplanar creatures cannot touch the recipient. Attacking a blocked creature in melee ends that. Reverse: guards against good creatures instead.

Ring of Hands/Ring of Woe.summary: Two to ten priests cast together and join hands, shielding everyone in the circle like protection from evil: evil attackers -1 and saves +1 per priest. The priests can't move or cast S/M spells and are attacked at +2. Reverse: guards against good instead.

Weighty Chest.summary: Enchants a non-living object up to a 5-ft cube; when anyone but you touches it, it becomes 1d4+1 times heavier than whoever is handling it. You can move it normally.

Wind Column.summary: Winds slow your fall according to the prevailing breeze: very strong or strong means no damage, moderate 1 per 10 ft (max 8), light 1d2 per 10 ft, still air 1d3 per 10 ft. Very strong wind can lift you up to 5 ft per level.

Create Holy Symbol.summary: Conjures a permanent holy symbol of your deity into your hands. It works for spells and turning undead like any other, or can be given to a junior priest of your faith.

Frisky Chest.summary: Enchants a non-living object up to a 10-ft cube: when anyone but you comes within 3 ft, it sprouts legs, wings or fins (move 24) and flees to 10 ft away. It can't attack or smash through barriers. Holding it for 1d4+1 rounds ends it.

Mystic Transfer.summary: For the rest of the turn you can receive a spell cast at you by a priest of your own deity and immediately cast it yourself or relay it onward, within its range. It works at the original caster's level; handling it takes your action.

Resist Acid and Corrosion.summary: Mild corrosives can't hurt the recipient, though gear can still suffer. Strong acids, including dragon breath and ooze attacks, do half damage; where a save applies, +3 to the save and damage drops to half on a failure, a quarter on a success.

Resist Fire/Resist Cold.summary: Choose fire or cold (the reverse form is simply the cold version): the recipient ignores mild exposure, and against intense or magical attacks of that kind gains +3 to saves and takes half damage, or a quarter if the save succeeds.

Withdraw.summary: Time slows for you alone: you get two rounds plus one per level to think while one round passes for others. You may only think, read, use divinations or heal yourself; you lose Dex and shield AC, and any successful hit ends it.

Zone of Truth.summary: Creatures in the area who fail a save cannot knowingly lie while inside it. They know they are affected, so they may stay silent or give evasive but truthful answers.
